newsitem.title: ITALY: Peruvian guerrilla's mother says son shot 30 times.
newsitem.headline: Peruvian guerrilla's mother says son shot 30 times.

text.p: The mother of dead Peruvian guerrilla leader Nestor Cerpa Cartolini said on Wednesday his head had been riddled with bullets during the storming of the Japanese ambassador's residence in Lima last month.
"In the case of my son, 30 bullets were found in his head," Felicitas Cartolini told a news conference in Rome. "The others were, however, completely blown to pieces."
Cerpa was killed on April 22 when Peruvian armed forces stormed the mansion where 14 Tupac Amaru Revolutionary Movement (MRTA) rebels had been holding 72 hostages for 126 days.
The military used firearms and bombs in a bloody 40-minute battle which left all the rebels dead. One hostage and two soldiers also died.

Cartolini, speaking in the Italian parliament building and accompanied by a daughter, said she wanted to condemn the violent end to the hostage crisis and highlight the continued holding of rebels in Peruvian jails.
"I am here in parliament to denounce the situation in Peru both in the prisons, where political prisoners are being held, and in the storming of the ambassador's residence," she said.
"The negotiations (for the hostages' release) were always in danger because there was no political will to get them going," she added.
Cerpa masterminded the seizure of the hostages to demand the release of 450 imprisoned guerrillas, including his wife who is serving life sentence on terrorism charges.
President Alberto Fujimori refused to yield ground and finally ordered the storming of the building.
Cartolini, who lives in a poor area of the French city of Nantes, looks after the couple's two small children.
She said her son and another rebel had been buried outside Lima but the fate of 12 other guerrillas was still unknown.
"The other 12 were put in plastic sacks and until now their families still do not know where they are buried," she said.
